title: A mode switch is scoped to one invocation; never let a flag leak into later commands
summary: When a one-off request needs JSON (or another mode) for exactly this command only, keep that switch scoped to the invocation and reset it when the call returns; an LLM's habit of flipping a global 'now output json' and leaving it on turns the whole later interactive session into a parser instead of a human prompt.
technique: Export a dynamic-scope variable for the duration of the single queue invocation and ensure it is removed/restored before the next command; non-interactive and interactive modes stay separate.
evidence_note: docs/BOB28_DIRECT_SOURCE_AND_JSON_CONTRACT.md:45 'stores the request in dynamically scoped QUEUEBASH_OUTPUT_JSON=1 for the duration of that queue invocation only. The global switch must not leak into later human commands.'
invariants: Tie a one-off mode flag to the scope/lifetime of that one invocation, not to the fish-wide session.
Restore or clear the mode before the next human command.
When exposing JSON mode, keep --help human and do not emit half-human help on the JSON channel.
Do not let non-interactive vs interactive behaviour share a lingering flag.
